result.scope_note: The claim is fully scoped, referring to the HTTP standard as of June 2022 with global applicability. The classification of HTTP methods, including PUT as idempotent, is defined in RFC 7231 and related standards, which were stable by that date.

explanation.text: The HTTP/1.1 specification updated in June 2022 via RFC 9110 classifies PUT as idempotent.
RFC 9110, titled 'HTTP Semantics,' was published by the IETF in June 2022 and is the authoritative source for HTTP method properties.
Span 423 from RFC 9110 shows PUT marked 'Yes' under the 'Idempotent' column in a methods table.
Spans 447 and 448 explicitly state that PUT is idempotent because successive identical requests are ignored.
The publication date of RFC 9110 is confirmed as June 2022 in the cited source.
The classification of PUT as idempotent in the June 2022 HTTP standard is supported by the authoritative IETF documentation.

The methods PUT and DELETE, and safe methods are defined as idempotent. Safe methods are trivially idempotent, since they are intended to have no effect on the server whatsoever; the PUT and DELETE methods, meanwhile, are idempotent since successive identical requests will be ignored.
